From “The Songs of Bilitis”LXI. Endearments

By Pierre Louÿs (1870–1925)

 
(1894. Translated from the French by Horace Manchester Brown. 1904)
C
LOSE
 softly thine arms about me like a girdle. Oh, touch, touch my skin thus! Neither water, nor the breath of the south wind are softer than thy hand.
  1

  To-day endear me, little sister, it is thy turn. Remember thou the endearments that I taught thee last night, and kneel thou near to me who am fatigued; kneel thou in silence.
  2

  Thy lips descend upon my lips. All thine undone hair follows them, as a caress follows a kiss. Thy locks glide upon my left breast; they hide thine eyes.
  3

  Give me thy hand, it is hot! Press mine and leave it not. Hands better than lips unite, and their passion is equalled by nothing.
  4
